title: t3: priority-max over 6 symbols, implemented as a stable sort
label: verified (local-full, full precision)
behavior: BOS + 6 tokens from {ba, gu, ku, po, se}; the model outputs one symbol at the last position.
summary: The model outputs the highest-priority symbol present in the input, with fixed priority po > gu > se > ba > ku, regardless of counts or positions. Internally it performs a full stable sort by that priority: mlp0 and mlp1 are both required before head 2.0; head 2.0 makes each position attend to BOS plus every position with a strictly lower sort key (ties broken by position), so its attention to BOS encodes 1/(1+rank); mlp2 is required between 2.0 and 3.1; head 3.1 at query position i attends with weight ~1 to the element of rank i-1 and copies its token, so the last position emits the largest element. Heads 0.0, 0.1, 1.0, 1.1, 2.1, 3.0 and mlp3 play no part. All numbers are from the local-full backend at full precision.
pseudocode:
prio = {ku:0, ba:1, se:2, gu:3, po:4}
# mlp0, mlp1: per-position sort key (priority, position as tiebreak)  [necessary; exact division of labour not resolved]
# head 2.0: rank[i] = #{j : key[j] < key[i]}   (attention to BOS = 1/(1+rank))
# mlp2: decode rank from the BOS-attention fraction
# head 3.1: out[i] = token at position with rank == i-1   (sorted sequence)
return max(tokens[1:], key=prio)   # value at the last position

claims.text: The model's output equals the highest-priority symbol present, priority po > gu > se > ba > ku, independent of counts and positions: 20/20 on hand-built prompts covering low-priority-only and single-minority cases, and 200/200 agreement on held-out prompts.
The model computes a deterministic function with logit difference ~1.0 on every prompt (accuracy 1.0 against its own labels).

Head 2.0 is necessary (mean ablation leaves 0.01% of the logit difference). It attends from each position to BOS and to every position with a strictly lower sort key, ties broken by earlier position; the opposite direction (attending to higher-priority symbols) was predicted and refuted.
mlp0, mlp1 and mlp2 are each necessary (mean ablation leaves <1% of the logit difference); mlp3 is not (100% remains).

Head 3.1 is the output head: zero-ablating it removes the logit difference entirely; at query position i it attends ~0.9999 to the single position holding the element of ascending rank i-1, so the last position reads the top-priority symbol.
Head 2.0 feeds head 3.1 through 3.1's key input (effect 0.34 with values still corrupt) and not through its query input (effect 0.0).
Heads 0.0, 0.1, 1.0, 1.1, 2.1, 3.0 and mlp3 play no part: jointly mean-ablating all seven leaves 100% of the logit difference.

The circuit {mlp0, mlp1, 2.0, mlp2, 3.1} is necessary and sufficient on held-out data: ablating it gives fraction -0.10 (accuracy 0.245); ablating everything else gives fraction 1.0 (accuracy 1.0); all null controls passed.

nodes.label: head 2.0: attend to BOS + lower keys (rank count)
head 3.1: position i copies element of rank i-1

limitations: The attention-pattern readings of 2.0 and 3.1 (E0008, E0009) rest on a single hand-built prompt; the full-sort description at non-final positions is not tested on outputs, since only the last position is read.
The benchmark dataset is dominated by po/gu answers; the order se > ba > ku rests on the 20 hand-built prompts in E0003.

The individual roles of mlp0 versus mlp1 and the mlp1->2.0 and 2.0->mlp2->3.1 edges through the MLPs were not path-patched (MLP senders failed in path_patching); they are inferred from necessity plus layer order.
The 2.0 -> 3.1 key path restores only 0.34 in a denoising patch, as expected when values stay corrupt, but the remainder was not separately attributed.
open_questions: What exactly do mlp0 and mlp1 each compute (priority lookup vs. position tiebreak)?
What do the inert heads (e.g. 1.1, 2.1, 3.0, which have sharp attention patterns) compute, given that they do not affect the output?

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: Head 2.0 is a comparison/counting head: each position attends to BOS plus every position holding a strictly higher-priority symbol, so the top symbol (po at position 2) attends only to BOS.

prediction.statement: 2.0 attention from position 2 (po, top priority) to BOS is at least 0.9
